body_html:
Losing a passport abroad involves the police, an embassy and Vietnam's Immigration Department, and the UK government names motorbike rental shops in its warning against leaving a passport as a guarantee, and Canada and Australia give general warnings against handing it to others. This guide collects what official pages say about where embassies are in Hanoi, what the US and British embassies advise after a loss, and why the UK, Canadian and Australian governments say to keep the passport in your own hands.

Only the US, British, Australian and Canadian pages could be read when checked on 24 October 2026, so lost-passport steps are given only for US and British travellers; travellers from elsewhere should look for their own embassy's guidance. Where a page shows no date, that is stated.

Where the embassies are

Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel) says embassies and consulates of foreign countries in Vietnam can be found in two cities, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs also publishes a list of foreign missions and their addresses through its Directorate of State Protocol, in Vietnamese. Neither page shows a date. The ministry list, as read for this article, is partial, and both use older phone-number and district formats, so neither is a safe source for phone numbers or opening hours. For example, the vietnam.travel list still shows Canada's Hanoi office at 31 Hung Vuong Street, which differs from the address on the Canadian government's page.

The reliable route is to find your own country's embassy on its official website and confirm the address and opening hours there. Three examples:

EmbassyAddress givenSource and date
United States, consular section for American citizensRose Garden Building, Second Floor, 170 Ngoc Khanh Street, Hanoi; mailing address 7 Lang Ha StreetU.S. Mission Vietnam, American Citizen Services FAQ; page shows no date
Australia8 Dao Tan Street, Ba Dinh District, HanoiAustralian Government Smartraveller, updated 24 September 2026
Canada22nd Floor, Tower 1, Capital Place Building, 29 Lieu Giai Street, HanoiGovernment of Canada travel advice, updated 19 October 2026

The ministry list gives the US embassy's address as 07 Láng Hạ, which matches the mailing address above, yet the consular section for American citizens is listed on a different street. That is why the embassy's own page matters; treat the table as a starting point.

If a passport is lost or stolen in Vietnam

Two embassy pages describe the steps for their own citizens, and both put the police report at the centre.

  • United States. The U.S. Embassy advises reporting a lost or stolen passport to the local Vietnamese police in the area where it happened, and says a passport reported lost or stolen is invalidated for travel. Apart from emergencies, American citizen services need an appointment booked in advance, and Vietnamese Immigration requires a police report before issuing the paperwork needed to leave the country.
  • United Kingdom. The British Embassy Hanoi says a lost or stolen passport has to be reported to the police station closest to where it is thought to have been lost, and that the police report must be shown at Immigration for the exit stamp.

Both pages show no date and cover only their own nationals; replacement-passport fees, processing times and the procedures of other countries are not covered by the sources reviewed.

Why a replacement passport still needs an exit step

The UK government's living-in-Vietnam guide, last updated 23 September 2025, states that Vietnamese Immigration requires the same passport to be used to enter and to leave the country. The same guide says a new passport or emergency travel document needs an exit visa stamp from Immigration, which it says can take between 3 and 7 days to be issued.

The British Embassy page gives a different figure. It says that leaving on an emergency travel document issued in Vietnam requires an exit visa from the Immigration Department, which can take up to 5 working days, and possibly longer after an overstay because the matter has to be investigated and a fine decided first. The two UK pages therefore give differently worded figures, so no single number is safe to plan around. The British Embassy page says the Immigration office can advise on the estimated processing time, which makes it the place to ask.

Why governments advise against handing over a passport

The UK government's Vietnam safety and security advice (this page shows no date) tells visitors not to give their passport to others as a guarantee, naming motorcycle rental shops and landlords, because they can hold it against claimed damage. It adds that a passport should not be used as a deposit for hiring vehicles, nor as a guarantee for paying a fine after a traffic offence.

Other governments give related, more general advice. Canada's travel advice, last updated 19 October 2026, lists "never leave your passport or any other ID document with anyone" as a hotel check-in tip, alongside asking for documents back as soon as check-in is complete. Australia's Smartraveller page, updated 24 September 2026, says not to let anyone trick you into handing the passport over and to keep it in a safe place.

What these pages do not say matters as well. None of the sources reviewed explains what Vietnamese law says about a shop, or anyone else, holding a passport, so nothing here should be read as saying that the practice is legal or illegal. The pages are advice from each government to its own travellers, not a description of any particular shop. Read beside the same-passport rule above, the practical concern is clear: leaving Vietnam depends on the passport used to enter.

For questions about passport security during a rental, see Passport Security During a Hanoi Motorbike Rental: Questions and Safer Records.

What to carry instead

The UK government advises keeping the passport and other valuables in a hotel or another secured location and carrying both photo and digital copies. It also says the authorities will accept a printed copy of the passport's photo page and visa as photographic ID. In practice that means three habits:

  1. Note your own embassy's address and opening hours from its official website before travelling.
  2. Keep a printed copy of the photo page and visa, and a digital copy stored apart from the passport.
  3. If the passport is lost or stolen, report it to the police station nearest to the loss, then contact the embassy and ask Immigration how long the exit step will take.

Before booking a rental, it helps to ask the shop in writing which documents it needs to see, whether anything is kept during the rental, and how and when it is returned. A ready-made message to adapt is available in A Motorbike Rental Booking Message for Hanoi: Copy-and-Send Template.

Embassy procedures and immigration rules change, so confirm every step with your embassy and the Immigration Department before relying on it.
